commits.message:
fix(docs): the live runtime reports a worker it cannot start, runs exporting code, and reloads in dev (rich-playground-afk.9c4)

- The frame's relay sends any failure to start the worker (a constructor
  that throws, a script that never loads) to the page as a crash, so the
  run can no longer be stuck in "running" or print "undefined".
- The playground program declares `exports`, the second CommonJS name
  Sucrase's output uses.
- The runtime module is bundled on every load and registers its files
  with addWatchFile, so docs:dev picks up edits to the worker and does not
  keep a failed bundle.

feat(docs): run visitor TypeScript in a sandboxed frame against a terminal (rich-playground-afk.9c4)

The playground's runner: a visitor's TypeScript becomes the script a live
terminal runs (theme/playground-program.ts), and every live terminal now runs
its program in a worker inside a frame sandboxed to an opaque origin.

- Types are stripped by Sucrase, chosen by weight on the page (minified,
  gzip -9): Sucrase 48 KB, typescript 1.0 MB, esbuild-wasm 3.7 MB. It keeps
  every line where it was, so an error's stack names the visitor's own line
  through a //# sourceURL.
- Imports by published name read the live library the docs' live examples
  already share (widgets and template-bindings with their optional peers).
- The worker's script is served as text (virtual:rich-live/runtime), since an
  opaque-origin frame can start a worker only from a script it holds. The
  worker reports every failure itself, with the error's stack.
- Stopping a run removes its frame, which ends a loop that never yields.

Verified in Chromium (e2e/playground-program.spec.ts): coloured Table,
animating Progress, Button on Enter, syntax and thrown errors at their lines,
a spinning program stopped with the page responsive and its worker gone, and
no document or origin inside the program. The docs' live examples pass
unchanged under the sandbox (e2e/live-examples.spec.ts).

fix(types): public declarations name no Node types (rich-types-42o) (#236)

* fix(types): public declarations name no Node types (rich-types-42o)

`ConsoleEnvironment.env`, `DetectColorOptions.env`, `RenderToStringOptions.env`
and `TerminalHost.env` were typed `NodeJS.ProcessEnv`, which the emitted .d.ts
carried verbatim; a project with no @types/node and skipLibCheck off failed on
them with `Cannot find namespace 'NodeJS'`. They now share `Env` (src/core/env.ts),
a read-only map from string to optional string that `process.env` satisfies
without a cast.

test/seam/browser-types.test.ts emits the declarations into a temp node_modules
and type-checks every non-node/ entry by its published specifier with
`types: []`; it fails with the five original errors on the old source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(types): the NodeJS probe imports every entry; fixtures name Env (rich-types-42o)

Review pass (high) on #236:
- The guard probe imported nothing, so Node types leaked through a symlinked
  peer's reference directive left it failing for the wrong reason. It now
  imports every browser entry first; reproduced with a scratch peer: old probe
  exit 2, new probe exit 0.
- Consumer tsconfig pins noUncheckedSideEffectImports rather than trusting
  TypeScript's default to make an unresolved entry an error.
- ambient-process.test.ts draws the airlock through isBehindNodeAirlock.
- Test fixtures standing in for the public API annotate Env, not ProcessEnv.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
